newsitem.title: USA: C-Cube sees strong demand for cheaper DVD.
newsitem.headline: C-Cube sees strong demand for cheaper DVD.

text.p: C-Cube Microsystems Inc chief executive Alex Balkanski said a new generation of affordably-priced digital videodisk (DVD) players should spark consumer demand in the second half of 1997.
Balkanski disputed a Fortune magazine article which said C-Cube faces dim prospects in the DVD market due to intense competition and consumer wariness about high prices.
"The current generation is too expensive," Balkanski said. "Once you break the $500 barrier and enter the $400 barrier, you should see tremendous price elasticity."
New products priced below $500 per unit will be released this summer, he said.
Balkanski said the market overreacted to the Fortune article, which he said "inadequately and incorrectly" portrayed the Milpitas, Calif.-based company.

"The future of DVD is just beginning. The transition is just starting. Within five to seven years, DVD will reach 100 percent of the population. All products based on video will be digital video products in the future," Balkanski said.
The Fortune article also suggested C-Cube was losing ground in the video compact disk market to rival ESS Technology Inc.
Balkanski said C-Cube has already reacted to this competition by cutting prices.

Balkanski sees the total video compact disk market growing from below seven milion units last year to about 10-14 million units in 1997. C-Cube expects to control more than half of the total video compact disk market this year.

Wall Street analysts expects C-Cube to earn $0.45 a share in the first quarter and $0.46 a share in the second quarter, according to First Call. These estimates are flat compared with fourth quarter earnings of $0.45 a share.
Balkanski declined to comment, citing a corporate policy of not commenting on Wall Street earnings forecasts.
C-Cube gained one to 26-3/4 on Thursday, regaining some of its recent losses.
